notes.title: The Zaoch Culture and its references
notes.content:
Zaoça is a country with many similarities to Brazil: A gigantic coastline, a diverse population, a strong culture, the love for football... But it also has its differences.

Starting with its origins. Although much of the north of Zaoça was the result of expeditions from the north of the ocean that landed on the coast, the country is currently a real mix of several different cultures. Before Zaoça, there were several villages that, 72 years ago, united around a religious messiah: Šäaik Klyte. The religion in question is Zoacism (don't confuse Zoacism - religion - with Zaoches - the people!), which can be categorized as polytheistic with prophets. Zoacism was important for the country's history and this will be addressed in another topic, but the fact is that there was no "independence" as in the Brazilian case.

Speaking a little deeper about the similarities, in addition to everything mentioned at the beginning of the text, there are also some iconic characters that are inspired by Brazilian celebrities. To name a few examples, we have:
[list]
[*] Cenoura Bravanel, one of the greatest presenters in the country who is inspired by Silvio Santos
[*] Cadu Galvão, a sports narrator who was inspired by Galvão Bueno (unfortunately already deceased due to old age in Zaoça...)
[*] Carlzalbé Videira, current coach of the Zaoch national football team, inspired by Carlos Alberto Parreira, coach of 4th Brazilian World Cup title at USA
[/list]

They and others will appear in the Alpyster app on Jæl's phone. Alpyster is a short messaging social network that is widely used throughout Yörvh. Eventually you will end up getting some notification about something that celebrities have been doing - including politicians - both from Zaoça and from other places on the planet as well.

About the climate, Brazil and Zaoça have many similarities as well. both have equator line cutting through their territory - although in the case of Zaoça it being much closer to the middle of the territory - making the tropical climate very similar in both countries. So no snow!

However, some regions have a milder climate, as in the state of Red Vinh, where the city of Walvoy is located. This region has an excellent mountain range for wine production. This is not present in Walvoy however, as it is a coastal town. A map of the region:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43530209/02c1b4975b73c156df514d7b3da2330fddf9b7dd.png[/img]

In addition, the capital of Zaoça, Yorvh Viax, was inaugurated about 25 years ago in the heart of its current territory, similar to Brasilia. Will Jæl make a visit there?

This was a sample of the general context of the country in which Jæl lives. In the next article, we'll dig a little deeper and talk about who Jæl is and who his family members are in Walvoy.

notes.title: Zaoça and its place on universe
notes.content:
[b]Zaoça: Šäaiks Lagush[/b] is the first game in a series that is supposed to be set in the country of Zaoça. Today we are going to talk a little about this country and the context in which it is inserted.

[h2]First of all, the origin of the story[/h2]

Zaoça was the name of a region in the old SimCity 4, which even gave rise to the Zaoça Journal in SimCity Brasil between 2009 and 2013 and a part of it is still available today in [url=https://community.simtropolis.com/forums/topic /39768-zaoça/]Simtropolis[/url].
The cities weren't really great... but several characters emerged with the creation of the União Brasileira de Regiões - UBR (Brazilian Union of Regions in free translate from Portuguese). The UBR's idea was to bring interactivity between the journal writers on the site, and from there came the universe where this game takes place, with some of its characters being born there.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43530209/6fb49eb83f6956332a0fcd96b8ad7c8e9fe84398.png[/img]

[h2]Astronomical context: Planet Yörvh[/h2]

The planet Yorvh (or [i]Yorṽ[/i] in the Zaoch spelling) is in a distant and fictional universe. It is approximately the size of our Moon and similar in composition to Earth, with vast oceans and 4 continents: Talammor, Kirm, Kwytia and Thotea.

Zaoça is located in the western part of Kwytia, in the region of the planet's equator and where it is agreed to be the main meridian for cartographic purposes, known as the Vinhalks Meridian, which passes close to the homonymous city where our protagonist will pass on his way to Walvoy.

About the technology, it is varied. Something mixed where cell phones and landlines coexist in a certain harmony, and where civil aviation has not yet taken off... Flights are very rare in Yorvh, perhaps due to some atmospheric condition they cannot stay more than 2 hours in the air.

There are other countries on the planet as well, but that can be a topic for another time.

[h2]Time context: Calendar of Seasons x Zaoch Calendar[/h2]
The Zaoch Calendar came about with the intention of creating more cycles during a year in the old UBR mentioned in the first part. There is a correlation with real time, but it won't be important in the game.

The game will start right after a controversial law is passed in the country, which resets the count of years and starts using a calendar of seasons as official. This is because of a recent past in Zaoça that is closely linked to religion, which has become traumatic for many of the current legislators - a subject for another text.

However, in the case of a tropical country, this new count is in doubt because it does not seem to make much sense, since the whole year has basically the same climate due to the proximity to the equator. We'll see in the game if this calendar has a future.

As this calendar will be very recent, there will still be some references to the old Zaoch Calendar. Some examples are the software used in the games at Casa de Jogos de Walvoy, which display all dates in Zaoch format.

The year 1 of the new calendar is equivalent to the year 241 of the Zaoch Calendar. We will have a text just to explain the reasons for this count of years.
